paragraphs.text: These are pieces of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) cakes pressed in the 1980s, broken apart rather than kept whole. The leaf is from Yunnan, and it was made in the style’s first two decades: the province’s state factories only brought the [wet-pile method](shou:wet-piling) into production in 1973.
Forty-one years on, the tea sits well beyond the ten years the trade looks for in [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). At this age the storage has shaped it as much as the years have.

brewing.text: Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
